recipe.title: Ginger–sesame tofu, broccoli & carrot bowls
recipe.description: A rice bowl with broccoli, carrots and a clearly defined sauce; choose one or three portions.
recipe.prepNote: Keep spring onion separate. For the roasted version, add sauce only at serving time to preserve the browned edges.
recipe.rationale: The rice is the base, the browned main adds bite, and the sauce and spring onion give the dish its flavour direction.
recipe.storageNote: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours; keep at 4°C or below. Eat within 2–3 days or freeze. Reheat cooked leftovers to 74°C.
recipe.source: Original Vibe Cooking personal seed pack v1 (2026-09-18). Not kitchen-tested. Times are estimates. Safety guidance: Health Canada; references and product-label limitations in the accompanying README.

servings.capacity: One 28 cm lidded frying pan and a small saucepan.

ingredients.preparation: firm; drain, pat dry, then cut into 2 cm cubes
dry weight; water for cooking is additional, according to the package
wash and cut into small florets
wash and cut into thin diagonal slices
divided between the main ingredient and vegetables
for the sauce; rice and steaming water are additional

steps.title: Prepare and start the rice
steps.instruction: Wash produce and prepare the listed ingredients. Cook 70 g dry rice using its package water ratio and timing. Pat tofu dry before cooking.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, ginger, listed sauce water, rice vinegar and sesame oil.

steps.title: Cook the main ingredient
steps.instruction: Heat half the oil in a 28 cm frying pan over medium-high heat, dividing it across 1 batch(es). Brown tofu in 1 batch(es), about 7–9 minutes each, turning to colour several sides. Transfer to a clean plate.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.instruction: Add the remaining oil, carrots and broccoli. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, add 30 ml extra water, cover and steam for 3–5 minutes until tender-crisp. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.instruction: Return the cooked main ingredient to the vegetables, add the sauce and toss over medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Add a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick. Serve with rice and spring onion.

recipe.title: Mustard–dill salmon, potatoes & greens
recipe.description: A fish-based batch with roasted potatoes, broccoli and a cool finishing sauce.
recipe.prepNote: Store the cooked fish and vegetables separately from the yoghurt sauce. Roast times assume the stated tray capacity.
recipe.rationale: The fish and potatoes stay familiar while the sauce and finishing herbs change the flavour.
safetyNotes: Cook fish to 70°C in its thickest part. Thaw in the refrigerator, and use separate tools for raw fish.
recipe.storageNote: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours; keep at 4°C or below. Eat within 2–3 days or freeze. Reheat cooked leftovers to 74°C.
recipe.source: Original Vibe Cooking personal seed pack v1 (2026-09-18). Not kitchen-tested. Times are estimates. Safety guidance: Health Canada; references and product-label limitations in the accompanying README.

servings.capacity: One large sheet pan and a separate small fish dish; a food thermometer.

ingredients.preparation: raw, boneless; fully thawed in the refrigerator
wash and cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss potatoes and carrots with two-thirds of the oil and the salt. Spread on one large sheet pan and roast for 20 minutes. Leave room for the broccoli later.

steps.title: Prepare the finish
steps.instruction: Mix yoghurt, Dijon and lemon juice; keep chilled. Reserve the dill.

steps.title: Add fish and broccoli
steps.instruction: Toss broccoli with the remaining oil and add to the vegetables. Place salmon in a separate small ovenproof dish. Roast alongside the vegetables for roughly 12–18 minutes, checking earlier for thin fillets. The thickest part of the salmon must reach 70°C on a thermometer; use temperature rather than time as the endpoint. Cook vegetables until tender, returning them to the oven separately if needed.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.instruction: Divide fish and vegetables into 1 portion(s). Add the chilled sauce and dill only when serving. Keep raw-fish tools away from the finished meal.

recipe.title: Tomato–herb lentil & spinach pasta
recipe.description: A canned-lentil dinner with carrots and spinach, designed for simple batch cooking.
recipe.prepNote: Use drained canned lentils, not the same weight of dry lentils. Keep fresh parsley separate. Freeze portions intended for later than the refrigerated window.
recipe.rationale: One simmered lentil foundation can move towards tomato and herbs or coconut, ginger and spices; the base changes too and is shown in the comparison.
recipe.storageNote: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours; keep at 4°C or below. Eat within 2–3 days or freeze. Reheat cooked leftovers to 74°C.

ingredients.preparation: drained and rinsed weight, not dry lentils
additional pasta-boiling water is not included

steps.title: Start the base
steps.instruction: Cook 75 g dry pasta in a separate saucepan, following the package instructions. Wash and prepare the vegetables.

steps.title: Soften the carrots
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a 2 litre saucepan. Add carrots and cook over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring. Add a small splash of the listed water if they stick.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.instruction: Add passata, the listed water, oregano and salt. Simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, until carrots are tender. Stir in the drained lentils and heat for 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the greens and finish
steps.instruction: Add spinach and cook for 2–3 minutes until wilted. Mix with cooked pasta, loosening with a little reserved pasta water if necessary. Divide into portions and finish with parsley.

steps.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the beaten eggs and fold gently with a spatula until set. Allow roughly 3–5 minutes. Cook the egg mixture to 74°C; timing varies by stove and pan.

steps.title: Serve or store the filling
steps.instruction: Warm each tortilla in a dry pan, divide the egg mixture between tortillas, add the mustard–herb sauce and roll tightly. For batch prep, cool and refrigerate the filling promptly, then toast or warm the bread and assemble only when eating.

recipe.title: Apple–cinnamon yoghurt crunch bowls
recipe.description: A cold breakfast base with a separate crunchy finish; one portion or three make-ahead breakfasts.
recipe.prepNote: Keep yoghurt, cooked apple and dry toppings separate. Slice banana just before eating. The three-portion profile is three breakfasts, not one larger breakfast.
recipe.rationale: Keeping toasted oats separate gives a texture change from soaked oats. The fruit and sauce set the flavour direction.
safetyNotes: Use pasteurised yoghurt and follow its after-opening directions. Ingredient records are not an allergy certification.
recipe.storageNote: Keep yoghurt refrigerated at 4°C or below and follow its label. Refrigerate cooked apple promptly. Plan these breakfasts within 2–3 days; add dry toppings and sliced banana when eating.
recipe.source: Original Vibe Cooking personal seed pack v1 (2026-09-18). Not kitchen-tested. Times are estimates. Safety guidance: Health Canada; references and product-label limitations in the accompanying README.

servings.capacity: A 24 cm dry pan, small saucepan and bowl.

ingredients.preparation: optional sweetness is included in the listed quantities

steps.title: Prepare the oats
steps.instruction: Toast 30 g oats in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently. Spread on a clean plate to cool. Keep dry oats separate from yoghurt until serving.

steps.title: Cook the fruit
steps.instruction: Put diced apple, cinnamon, listed water and maple syrup in a small covered saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until tender. Add a small splash of water only if needed. For storing, transfer fruit to a shallow container and refrigerate promptly, separate from yoghurt.

steps.title: Build the bowl
steps.instruction: Divide yoghurt into 1 bowl(s) or containers. At serving, add apple, cooled toasted oats and walnuts. Serve the fruit slightly warm or chilled; do not mix hot fruit into yoghurt intended for storage.
